# Modifications

This is gpui 0.2.2 from crates.io, changed by qol-tools:

- `src/elements/text.rs`: each measure of a text element truncates a copy of its runs, so a narrow measure no longer shortens what a later, wider layout draws. Zed fixed the same bug upstream in zed-industries/zed#45122.
- `src/text_system.rs`: `line_clamp` counts each hard line break as a line. It counted only wrapped lines, so a clamped text with line breaks drew every paragraph past its clamp, and a two-line toast detail holding a multi-paragraph report overflowed the card. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/taffy.rs`: the grid repeat names its float literals `f32`, as Zed does upstream, so newer compilers do not reject the fallback to `f32`.
- `src/window.rs`: when the platform reports a resize or move while the app is already borrowed, the window reads its new bounds once that update returns instead of dropping them, and several reports before then share one deferred read. qol code sets a native window frame synchronously inside an update, and gpui used to keep the stale viewport and scale and log `RefCell already borrowed`.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`: a new window is created at its requested origin (no 2 px shift) and WM_NORMAL_HINTS carries that origin and size as user-specified with static gravity, so Muffin and other window managers map it there instead of placing it and moving it after the first map, and a restored inner bounds lands exactly. Upstream gpui still sets only the minimum size; this is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`: an X11 window returns its XCB window and display handles instead of panicking with `unimplemented!()`, as Zed does upstream since zed-industries/zed#50768. qol code reads the connection from the display handle to grab the keyboard on gpui's own connection while the alt-tab picker is open, so the keys reach the picker and the desktop's own shortcuts cannot open under it.
- The `examples` and `docs` folders and the `[[example]]` targets are removed.
- `src/app/test_context.rs` and `src/platform/test/window.rs`: expose the fake window handle and add simulated moves so workspace regression tests can deliver resize/move callbacks during an app update. The tests cover deferred bounds, coalescing, subsequent immediate updates, and closing a window before deferred work runs.
- `src/platform/windows/keyboard.rs`: the AltGr layout list adds Danish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Icelandic, Belgian French, Swiss German, Swiss French, Croatian, Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Greek and Bulgarian, so `@ $ { [ ] }` type on a Danish layout.
- `src/platform/windows/direct_write.rs`: when a family name matches no font by its weight-stretch-style (WSS) family name, the lookup retries with the WSS name of a font whose typographic family has that name. It prefers the WSS name equal to the typographic name, otherwise the face closest to the requested weight, stretch and style. A font whose faces carry a WSS family that differs from its typographic family could not load by its typographic name, because DirectWrite's `GetMatchingFonts` only matches the WSS name. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` sends its synthetic Alt press and release only while Alt is up. A held Alt already lets the process take the foreground, and the injected release made a hold-to-switch picker opened by Alt+Tab read Alt as released and close at once.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window opened hidden keeps the on-screen position the app gave it when it is first activated. gpui used to re-apply the placement it stored at creation, so a hidden preview that qol moved next to the cursor jumped back to where it was created on its first show. A window opened hidden also takes its placement's frame at creation, as a shown window does: it was created with its content size as its frame size, so a hidden panel kept a content area smaller than it asked for.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a new window is created at its requested bounds, converted with its target display's scale, so it starts on that display at that display's DPI. gpui created it on the primary display and converted the bounds with the primary display's scale, so a window opened on a display with another scale landed at the wrong origin and Windows grew it by the ratio of the two scales when it moved there.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: the window frame offsets keep the measured left and top insets, so a window placed or resized at client bounds puts its client exactly there. gpui split the frame evenly between top and bottom, but a window without a native title bar has a 1 to 2 px top inset and an 8 to 11 px bottom one, so every placement and resize moved the client up 3 to 4 px and a remembered window crept upward on each reopen.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`: a window gpui has dropped no longer calls back into gpui. gpui destroys a dropped window later on its executor, and what reached it in between (hit tests, key releases, paints, the deactivation sent while it is destroyed) was handed to a window gpui no longer had, so every closed window logged `window not found` errors.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` logs `SetActiveWindow` and `SetFocus` only when they fail. Both return the previously active or focused window, so a window activated while the app had none logged an error with the code for success.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `resize` keeps the window's activation and stacking. gpui resized with a plain `SetWindowPos`, which also raises and activates the window, so a resize could take the keyboard from another window: shrinking the hidden shot preview after it opened the editor left the editor without keys. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window opened visible with `focus: false` is shown without being activated, as Zed does upstream since zed-industries/zed#61411. gpui showed every new window with `SW_SHOWNORMAL`, which activates it, so a toast took the keyboard from the window the user was in: the tray's "Screenshot saved" toast took focus from the shot preview that opened with it.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a `PopUp` window is created topmost, as its documentation promises and as macOS does by raising it to the pop-up window level. gpui gave it only the tool window style, so a toast opened behind a maximized window and was never seen. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: `activate` taps an unassigned key between its synthetic Alt press and release. A lone Alt reaches the window that still has the keyboard and puts it into menu mode, so the first Settings window after the tray started left Notepad behind it showing its menu key tips, and the next letter typed into Notepad opened a menu instead. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a `Floating` window is owned by the app's active window when it opens, as X11 makes it transient for the focused window and Wayland gives it that parent. gpui opened it as an unowned app window, so qol's color wheel added a second, untitled window to the taskbar button and nothing kept it above the settings window it belongs to. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/system_settings.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: a window asks the taskbar whether it auto-hides only once it is maximized, and again after the work area changes, instead of each time a window is created. The question waits on Explorer, so while Explorer's taskbar hung, no window could open until Explorer recovered. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`: text typed as Unicode packets (`VK_PACKET`), which input tools send through `SendInput` with `KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`, reaches a window without a text input handler as key-down keystrokes, the way typed keys do. gpui handed that text only to an input handler, so views that read keystrokes, such as qol's search fields, never saw it.
- `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/windows/keyboard.rs`: a keystroke's `key_char` is the text the key types, as on Linux and macOS. The space key types a space, and a dead key types nothing until the key after it completes the character. gpui gave the space key no `key_char` and gave a dead key its accent, so views that read `key_char`, such as qol's search fields, dropped every space and typed `café` as `caf'é`.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`: a window that another client destroys, as `xdotool windowclose` does, closes the same way as a window the user closes, so the app quits with its last window. gpui ignored `DestroyNotify`, kept the dead window in its list and never stopped its event loop, so the process stayed alive with no window and logged `BadWindow` errors. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`, `src/platform/blade/blade_renderer.rs`, `src/platform/blade/shaders.wgsl`, `src/platform/blade/apple_compat.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`: a window opened with `window_min_size` renders into a child window whose swapchain is sized apart from the window. At rest the child holds the content rounded up to 256 px. When a live resize starts (`start_window_resize`, `Window::expect_live_resize`, or a configure that answers a `_NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST`) it grows once to the largest monitor, and its swapchain keeps that size for the rest of the window's life, so the drag steps rebuild nothing. A programmatic resize that outgrows the child grows it to the content in 256 px steps. It never shrinks and never passes 8192 px on either axis. The window's content size is tracked separately as `content_extent`. `BladeSurfaceConfig` gains `content_size` (`None` on Wayland and macOS, where the drawable is the content) and `BladeRenderer` gains `update_render_size(drawable, content)`. The path intermediate and MSAA textures follow the content size in 256 px steps instead of the drawable, and the path shader samples them by their own size. Exposure events on the child count as exposures of the window. Rebuilding the swapchain on every resize step made resizing a qol panel stutter, and a monitor-sized swapchain on every resizable window cost about 100 MB per 4K window even when it was hidden and never resized. After a live resize each frame clears the whole monitor-sized image, which costs memory bandwidth on software renderers. Windows that declare no minimum (keepalives, pickers, previews, the color wheel) render straight into their own window as before. This is specific to qol's resizable panels and not an upstream candidate as is.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`: content size reads `content_extent` instead of the renderer's viewport, because the viewport is now the larger render child. Delete with the render child above.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`: the `_NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST` counter of a resize is acked on the refresh after the frame drawn at the new size, instead of as soon as the configure arrives. A move-only configure still acks at once and drops any older value still parked, so the counter never moves backwards. The request, park and ack steps live in `SyncAck`. Acking before the new frame let the window manager show the next resize step over a stale frame. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`: `_NET_WM_MOVERESIZE` starts at the root position of the button press that began the drag, kept from `XinputButtonPress` until the release or until one move or resize uses it, and falls back to `QueryPointer` when there is none. Querying the pointer when the message is sent anchored the drag where the pointer had already moved to, so a quick drag on a resize edge jumped by that distance. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/window.rs`, `src/platform.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`, `src/platform/mac/window.rs`: `Window::set_window_min_size` changes the minimum content size of an open window. X11 rewrites WM_NORMAL_HINTS with the same builder as window creation, so the static gravity and the user-specified position and size stay, and both write the minimum in device pixels (upstream wrote logical pixels, half the minimum at scale 2); Windows sets the minimum that `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` already reads; macOS calls `setContentMinSize`; Wayland sets the xdg toplevel minimum; other platforms ignore it. qol panels change their minimum as they fold or switch pages, and setting it from outside gpui by window title overwrote gpui's own size hints on X11 and needed a window procedure subclass on Windows. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/window.rs`, `src/platform.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/wayland/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform/mac/window.rs`: `Window::is_live_resizing` reports whether the user is resizing the window through the operating system: X11 a resize configure that answers a `_NET_WM_SYNC_REQUEST`, Windows the `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` loop, Wayland the xdg toplevel resizing state, macOS `inLiveResize`. `Window::expect_live_resize` lets a window that moves its own edges grow the X11 render child before the first step, and is a no-op elsewhere. qol surfaces remember a size only when the user made it, and a resize from the window frame, a keyboard resize or a window-manager binding had no other evidence. This is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/mac/window.rs`: `WindowOptions::icon` sets an X11 window's `_NET_WM_ICON`, as Zed does upstream since zed-industries/zed#40096, so a panel or window list shows the app's own icon instead of the desktop's fallback. Other platforms ignore it.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/drag_out.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`, `src/platform/linux/x11/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/window.rs`, `src/platform/windows/events.rs`, `src/platform.rs`, `src/window.rs`: `Window::offer_dragged_paths` lets a drag started inside the window carry files out to other apps. While the button is held and the pointer is outside the window, the X11 backend acts as an XDND source: it finds the XdndAware window under the pointer (following XdndProxy), sends enter, position, leave and drop, and answers the XdndSelection request with a `text/uri-list` (plus `TARGETS`). Shift asks for a move, otherwise a copy, and the target performs it. An optional `DragImage` rides beside the pointer outside the window in an override-redirect 32-bit window whose background is the premultiplied picture, placed off the hotspot so target lookup never hits it; inside the window it hides and the app draws its own drag view. While the target under the pointer accepts a copy, the window's cursor (which X shows during the implicit button grab) becomes the copy cursor, and it returns to the window's own style otherwise. Inside the window the drag stays an ordinary gpui drag. On Windows the offer is kept while the left button is held, and when the pointer leaves the client area the window posts itself `WM_GPUI_DRAG_OUT` and runs OLE `DoDragDrop` with no borrows held. The data object comes from the shell (`SHParseDisplayName`, `SHCreateShellItemArrayFromIDLists`, `BHID_DataObject`), so it carries `CF_HDROP` and shell IDLists. Copy and move are both allowed and the target chooses; gpui never deletes the source. The drop source cancels on Escape, drops on left button up and keeps Windows' own cursors. The `DragImage` goes to `IDragSourceHelper2` as a premultiplied top-down DIB padded by the offset, with drop description text enabled. While the drag is over the window itself, the drop target feeds gpui mouse moves with the left button down, answers `DROPEFFECT_NONE` and turns the drop into a mouse up, so the internal drag continues. When `DoDragDrop` returns any other way gpui gets a mouse up at the pointer. Other backends ignore the call. Upstream gpui has no drag source; this is an upstream candidate for zed-industries/zed.
- `src/platform/linux/x11/client.rs`: a file drop reads the whole `text/uri-list` property. gpui read at most 1024 32-bit units (4 KB), so a drop of many files from another app silently lost every path past the first 4 KB.
